data.current_summary: Disputes on your tasks
data.current_description: A worker who thinks a refusal was wrong can dispute it, once per proof. On a refusal YOU made (`refusal.by` `you`) you decide first: pay the worker (POST /disputes/{id}/accept), keep your refusal (POST /disputes/{id}/uphold) or let them send it again (POST /disputes/{id}/send-back). If nobody decides by `decide_by` (48 hours after it opened), our automatic look decides. It reads your refusal's reason beside the worker's words, and does not approve over a specific reason it cannot check itself (a code you gave out, your own records, an account that already did the work). Unless it finds the work done, your refusal stands. When it does: a task with a `verify_url` is asked once more — event `dispute.check` (header `Microworker-Event`), signed like `proof.check`, body `{ "event": "dispute.check", "task_id", "submission_id", "dispute_id", "worker_ref", "proof": { "text", "url" }, "refusal": { "reason" }, "dispute": { "reason" } }`, answered within 5 seconds — and `{ "valid": false, "reason": "…" }` keeps your refusal (the worker reads your reason), `{ "valid": true }` pays the worker. With no clear answer (or no `verify_url`), a refusal you gave a reason for is not paid: it waits for our staff (`waiting_for` `staff`, `staff_review`), and your refusal stands by itself at the new `decide_by` (48 hours later). You can still decide it yourself meanwhile. A refusal without a reason is paid. A refusal our automatic review made (`automatic`) is decided by that look within moments — when it finds only something missing, it lets the worker send it again by itself (`sent_back`); you may still pay it or send it back; one our staff made (`staff`) is decided by our staff. `can_accept`, `can_uphold` and `can_send_back` say what you can do now. `automatic_look` is what our look found (advice until the time runs out). Open disputes by default; `status=all` includes decided ones. The webhooks `dispute.opened` and `dispute.decided` carry the same object.
data.summary_suggestion: List disputes on your submissions
data.description_suggestion: Retrieve disputes on your task submissions. Workers can dispute refusals once per proof. For refusals you made, you can accept (pay worker), uphold (keep refusal), or send back (allow resubmission) within 48 hours. If undecided, automatic review decides: it may uphold your refusal, send back for resubmission, or (if task has verify_url) trigger a dispute.check webhook for your verification. Refusals with reasons that automatic review cannot verify wait for staff review. Refusals without reasons are auto-paid. Refusals by automatic or staff review are decided by those systems. Response includes `can_accept`, `can_uphold`, `can_send_back` flags and `automatic_look` advice. Filter with `status=all` to include decided disputes. Returns array of dispute objects.

data.current_summary: Pay the worker: decide a dispute for them
data.current_description: On your own task: the worker was right — Microworker pays the worker after all, charged to the task's budget (a cancelled task kept a reserve for it), and the dispute is decided for the worker. On a refusal you made or one our automatic review made; not on one our staff made (409 `dispute_staff_refusal`), nor on a proof our checks or staff found fake (409 `dispute_fake_proof`), nor on a task paid with free credit (409 `credit_job_review`: our team decides those). A dispute already decided the same way answers again with `duplicate: true`.
data.summary_suggestion: Accept dispute and pay the worker
data.description_suggestion: Accept a dispute on your own task, deciding in the worker's favor. Microworker pays the worker from the task's budget (or from a reserve if task is cancelled). Can only be used on disputes for refusals you made or automatic review made (409 `dispute_staff_refusal` for staff refusals, 409 `dispute_fake_proof` for fake proofs, 409 `credit_job_review` for free credit tasks). If the dispute was already decided the same way, returns `duplicate: true`. Returns the updated dispute with accepted status.

data.current_description: A worker who thinks a refusal was wrong can dispute it, once per proof. On a refusal YOU made (`refusal.by` `you`) you decide first: pay the worker (POST /disputes/{id}/accept), keep your refusal (POST /disputes/{id}/uphold) or let them send it again (POST /disputes/{id}/send-back). If nobody decides by `decide_by` (48 hours after it opened), our automatic look decides. It reads your refusal's reason beside the worker's words, and does not approve over a specific reason it cannot check itself (a code you gave out, your own records, an account that already did the work). Unless it finds the work done, your refusal stands. When it does: a task with a `verify_url` is asked once more — event `dispute.check` (header `Microworker-Event`), signed like `proof.check`, body `{ "event": "dispute.check", "task_id", "submission_id", "dispute_id", "worker_ref", "proof": { "text", "url" }, "refusal": { "reason" }, "dispute": { "reason" } }`, answered within 5 seconds — and `{ "valid": false, "reason": "…" }` keeps your refusal (the worker reads your reason), `{ "valid": true }` pays the worker. With no clear answer (or no `verify_url`), a refusal you gave a reason for is not paid: it waits for our staff (`waiting_for` `staff`, `staff_review`), and your refusal stands by itself at the new `decide_by` (48 hours later). You can still decide it yourself meanwhile. A refusal without a reason is paid. A refusal our automatic review made (`automatic`) is decided by that look within moments — when it finds only something missing, it lets the worker send it again by itself (`sent_back`); you may still pay it or send it back; one our staff made (`staff`) is decided by our staff. `can_accept`, `can_uphold` and `can_send_back` say what you can do now. `automatic_look` is what our look found (advice until the time runs out).
